intro: A five course menu built around game: wild boar, elk and duck. Each course is named for how it is cooked, raw, braised, seared and baked, and the menu runs from a one bite boar chop to a dessert made with duck fat. Japanese technique turns up early, with a yakitori glaze, furikake and a tataki, before the menu moves to Italy and the American South.

courses.name: Wild Boar Chop
courses.tableside: A one bite wild boar chop to open the menu. It's lacquered with a yakitori style barbecue glaze, sweet and salty from soy and mirin, and finished with a furikake made from cornbread. Japanese seasoning on a Southern base, which sets up the rest of the menu.

shellfish.note: No shellfish expected. Some furikake blends include dried shrimp. Confirm.

dairy.note: Cornbread is usually made with butter or buttermilk. Confirm.

gluten.note: Yakitori glaze is soy sauce based, and cornbread usually contains wheat flour.

key_terms.definition: Japanese skewered chicken grilled over charcoal. The glaze, called tare, is a reduction of soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar, brushed on repeatedly so it builds into a lacquer.
A dry Japanese seasoning sprinkled over rice, usually built on toasted sesame, nori, salt and sugar, and often dried bonito. Here the base is crumbled cornbread.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pig. Leaner and darker than pork, with a deeper, slightly nutty flavour because the animals forage and move far more.

courses.chef_notes: One bite. Introduce the game theme as it lands. Allergens the grid does not track: furikake is typically sesame based and often contains bonito, so ask the kitchen for a guest with a sesame or fish allergy.

courses.name: Elk Tataki
courses.description: Smoked ponzu, soy pearls, sriracha aioli, scallion
courses.tableside: Elk seared for a few seconds on the outside and left raw through the middle, then sliced thin. It sits in a smoked ponzu, a citrus soy sauce, with little pearls of soy, a sriracha aioli and scallion. Elk is lean and clean tasting, closer to beef than to venison.

gluten.note: Ponzu and soy pearls are soy sauce based, which contains wheat unless made with tamari.

eggs.note: Aioli is egg yolk based. Ask whether it can come off.

key_terms.definition: A Japanese technique: meat or fish seared very briefly over high heat, chilled, then sliced thin so the outside is cooked and the inside raw. The word means pounded or hit.
A Japanese sauce of citrus juice, soy sauce, mirin and rice vinegar, traditionally steeped with kombu and bonito flakes. The name comes from the Dutch pons, meaning punch.
Soy sauce set into small beads, usually with a seaweed derived gelling agent, so they burst on the tongue. The same idea as caviar, with soy in place of roe.
A large North American deer. The meat is very lean and mild, with less of the iron edge people expect from venison, which is why it works served raw.

courses.chef_notes: Raw course, so give the undercooked meat advisory when a guest asks. Traditional ponzu contains bonito, which matters for a fish allergy even though the grid does not track fish. Confirm with the kitchen.

pairing.name: Cabernet Sauvignon Rosé Sekt Reserve
pairing.note: A dry Austrian rosé Sekt made from Cabernet Sauvignon, with strawberry, rose hip and light red cherry. Red fruit is what lets a sparkling wine sit next to raw red meat: lean elk has a faint iron edge that a white would sharpen and this softens. The bubbles and acidity scrub the sriracha aioli off the palate, and because the wine is fully dry it stays clean against the salt and citrus of the ponzu instead of turning sweet. Cabernet keeps a little savoury grip even as a rosé, which gives it enough body for meat rather than fish. Also on our sparkling list by the bottle.

courses._verify: Printed menu pours the 2024. wines.json #102 lists the 2023. Confirm which vintage is in the cellar and update one or the other.

courses.name: Wild Boar Ragu
courses.description: Okinawan sweet potato gnocchi, brie fonduta, trumpet mushroom, sage crumble
courses.tableside: Wild boar braised down into a ragu, served over gnocchi made from Okinawan sweet potato, which is purple inside. There's a brie fonduta, a melted cheese sauce, with trumpet mushrooms and a crumble of sage on top. The richest course on the menu.

nuts.note: No tree nuts expected. Confirm the sage crumble.

gluten.note: Gnocchi is bound with wheat flour, and the crumble is likely bread or flour based.

eggs.note: Gnocchi dough and fonduta can both use egg. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: A sweet potato with pale skin and deep purple flesh, the colour coming from anthocyanins. Drier, denser and less sugary than an orange sweet potato, which makes it good for gnocchi.
The Italian cousin of fondue, from Piedmont and the Aosta Valley, traditionally Fontina melted with milk, butter and egg yolk. This one is made with brie.
King trumpet, the largest of the oyster mushroom family. Thick white stem, small cap, and a meaty texture that holds up in a braise.
An Italian meat sauce cooked slowly until the meat breaks down. Bolognese is the best known, but the word covers any long cooked meat sauce.

courses.chef_notes: Gluten and dairy are both structural here. Egg is the open question: ask whether the gnocchi and the fonduta use it before answering an egg allergy.

pairing.name: 'Basadone' Pelaverga, Verduno
pairing.note: Pelaverga is light, silky and perfumed: rose petal, white cherry, cranberry and a distinct white pepper note, at about 13 percent alcohol. It works by contrast. The ragu, the brie fonduta and the sweet potato gnocchi are all soft and rich, and the wine's acidity and pepper cut through them where a heavier red would add more weight to an already heavy course. Low tannin means nothing clashes with the sweetness of the gnocchi, and the tart red fruit lifts the braised boar. The grape is grown almost only in the commune of Verduno, next to Barolo. The printed menu spells it Pelavagra. Also on our list by the bottle.

courses.name: Pistachio Crusted Duck Breast
courses.description: Crispy duck confit, collard greens, sour cherry demi-glace
courses.tableside: Duck two ways. A seared breast with a pistachio crust, served pink, alongside crispy duck confit, which is leg meat slow cooked in its own fat. Collard greens and a sour cherry demi-glace finish the plate. Pistachio is on the outside of the breast, so mention it.

dairy.note: Collards and the demi are often finished with butter. Confirm.

gluten.note: Confirm whether the crust uses a flour or breadcrumb binder, and whether the confit is dusted before crisping.

eggs.note: Crusts are often bound with egg. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: From the French confire, to preserve. Duck legs are salt cured, then cooked slowly submerged in duck fat until tender. Crisped before serving.
A classical French sauce built by reducing veal or beef stock with wine until it is glossy and coats a spoon. Sour cherry gives this one acidity to cut the duck fat.
A sturdy leafy green in the cabbage family and a staple of Southern cooking, usually braised until tender. Slightly bitter, which balances rich meat.

courses.chef_notes: Pistachio is the obvious nut allergen and cannot be hidden, since it is on the outside of the breast. Ask whether the breast can go out without the crust. Collards in Southern cooking are often braised with pork, so confirm for a guest avoiding pork.

pairing.name: Petite Sirah, Lytton Estate, Sonoma County
pairing.note: Inky and dense, with blackberry, dark chocolate and black pepper over firm tannin. Two kinds of duck fat on one plate, crisp confit and a rendered breast, need that much tannin to cut through them. The wine's dark fruit sits alongside the sour cherry demi rather than competing with it, and the pepper meets the bitterness of the collards. The printed menu says Petit Syrah. The grape is Petite Sirah, also called Durif, and it is not the same grape as Syrah. Also on our list by the bottle.

courses.name: Duck Fat Apple Tart
courses.description: Niman Ranch bacon, salted caramel, candied pecans, Buffalo Trace ice cream
courses.tableside: An apple tart with the pastry made with duck fat, which keeps the game theme running into dessert. It's topped with Niman Ranch bacon, salted caramel and candied pecans, with ice cream made with Buffalo Trace bourbon. Sweet and salty, and not one for a vegetarian.

eggs.note: Ice cream is usually a custard base. Confirm the ice cream and pastry.

key_terms.definition: Pastry made with rendered duck fat in place of some or all of the butter. It bakes up flaky the way lard pastry does, with a savoury edge that suits apple and bacon.

A Quebec born dessert drink made from apple juice concentrated by freezing, either by pressing frozen apples or by leaving pressed juice outside in winter so the water freezes off. The pairing on this course.

sourcing.name: Niman Ranch
sourcing.description: A network of independent American family farms. Its pork is raised without antibiotics or added hormones.

sourcing.name: Buffalo Trace
sourcing.description: Bourbon from the Buffalo Trace Distillery in Frankfort, Kentucky. The same bourbon is on our whisky list, which is an easy suggestion for a guest who wants a glass after dinner.

courses.chef_notes: Not vegetarian in two ways: duck fat in the pastry and bacon on top. Bacon can presumably come off but the pastry cannot change. The ice cream is made with bourbon, so flag it for a guest avoiding alcohol. Pecans are on the plate.

pairing.name: Heirloom Blend Ice Cider
pairing.note: Ice cider made from a blend of heirloom Vermont apples, with the juice concentrated by winter cold before fermentation. Very sweet but with high acidity, so it reads as concentrated baked apple rather than syrup. Apple against apple is the obvious link, but the acidity does the work: it cuts the duck fat pastry and the salted caramel so the course does not cloy, and it is sweet enough to match the dessert without tasting thin beside it. Eden was Vermont's first ice cider producer, started in 2007 by Eleanor and Albert Leger on a former dairy farm. Not on our regular list.
